title: Default Market Offer price cap (NSW, SEQ, SA)
summary: A mandatory Electricity Retail Code introduced a Default Market Offer cap on standing offers and a reference price for advertising discounts in NSW, south-east Queensland and South Australia from 1 July 2019.

instruments.title: Competition and Consumer (Industry Code—Electricity Retail) Regulations 2019

direction_rationale: A cap on standing offers may compress retail margins and deter entry, while a common reference price improves comparability of offers and consumer switching.

industries.name: On Selling Electricity and Electricity Market Operation

comparison: Regional Queensland, Tasmania and ACT (regulated prices, no DMO); Victoria has its own VDO on the same date
price_series: Electricity; Gas and other household fuels
notes: Applies in three jurisdictions on one date; jurisdiction coded CTH because the instrument is Commonwealth.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Caps standing-offer electricity prices in New South Wales, south-east Queensland and South Australia, and makes retailers quote discounts against the same reference price. It protects customers who do not shop around, but a regulated price can compress the margins entrants rely on.

marks.reason: A regulated default price replaces retailer-set standing offers and may sit away from some retailers' costs.
A common reference price makes offers easier to compare and curbs the 'loyalty tax' on customers who do not switch.
Lower standing-offer margins can deter smaller retailers from entering or expanding.
